variants.title: Today
variants.desc: The live rating system, unchanged: OpenSkill per round with damping 4 and a cap of 150 per match. The baseline every other proposal is compared with.

variants.title: Pairwise Elo
variants.desc: Each round counts as a win against everyone you finished above and a loss against everyone below, weighted so a round is worth the same in any lobby size. The step shrinks from 1 to 0.03 over the first rounds (e^(−rounds/20)), so new players settle fast and regulars stay steady. New players start 2 units below the median regular (50+ rounds), shown as 1000, so a regular is about 1560. Caps per match: 150 points, 400 under 50 rounds. Under 20 rounds the board shows only rounds/20 of a player's gain (the rating itself is not cut), so a lucky first match can't put someone at the top.

variants.title: Pairwise Elo, no caps
variants.desc: Pairwise Elo without caps or the provisional display. Predicts a little better, but a one-match alt can jump to the top 3.

variants.title: Glicko-style
variants.desc: Pairwise like Pairwise Elo, but each player has an uncertainty that shrinks as they play: unsure ratings move a lot, sure ones little. New players start 1.5 units below the median regular (50+ rounds), shown as 1000, so a regular is about 1560. Caps per match: 150 points, 400 under 50 rounds.

variants.title: Plackett-Luce Elo
variants.desc: Updates on the chance of the whole finishing order (the model today's system uses) instead of pairs, with a step that shrinks over the first rounds. New players start 1.5 units below the median regular (50+ rounds), shown as 1000, so a regular is about 1560. Caps per match: 150 points, 400 under 50 rounds.

variants.title: Match Elo
variants.desc: Pairwise Elo, but every round of a match is judged on the ratings at its start, so a streak inside one match doesn't snowball. New players start 2 units below the median regular (50+ rounds), shown as 1000, so a regular is about 1560. Caps per match: 150 points, 400 under 50 rounds.

variants.title: OpenSkill, no damping
variants.desc: Today's system without the damping and without the cap: each round moves the rating by OpenSkill's full amount.

variants.title: Anchored start
variants.desc: Today's OpenSkill, but new players start 8 units (560 points) below the median regular, shown as 1000. For their first 100 rounds they move up to 2× faster, and under 50 rounds the cap is 400 instead of 150.

variants.title: Anchored start, 10 below
variants.desc: The anchored start, with new players 10 units (700 points) below the median regular.

variants.title: Faster newcomers, normal start
variants.desc: New players move up to 2× faster over their first 100 rounds and have a 400 cap under 50 rounds. They start at 1000 like today.

variants.title: Faster newcomers only
variants.desc: New players move up to 2× faster over their first 100 rounds. Nothing else changes.

variants.title: Anchored start + trust 20
variants.desc: The anchored start and the trust rule (gains from beating a player scaled by their trust, full at 20 rounds).

variants.title: Anchored start + trust, from now on
variants.desc: The anchored start and the trust rule as last proposed (10% on the first round, full at 10, newcomers rated normally), switched on at the start of the choice slice.

variants.title: Trust 20, everyone
variants.desc: Your gain from a round is multiplied by the average trust of the players you beat: 0% for a brand new player, 100% from 20 rounds. Losses stay the same.

variants.title: Trust 20, 20+ round players only
variants.desc: The trust rule, but only for players who already have 20+ rounds.

variants.title: Trust 10
variants.desc: The trust rule with full trust at 10 rounds.

variants.title: Trust 40
variants.desc: The trust rule with full trust at 40 rounds.

variants.title: 10% first round, full at 10
variants.desc: Trust starts at 10% on a player's first round and is full at round 10.

variants.title: Newcomers rated normally
variants.desc: 10% first round, full at 10, and newcomers' own gains aren't cut: only players with 10+ rounds gain less from beating them.

variants.title: Newcomers rated normally, from now on
variants.desc: The same, switched on at the start of the choice slice instead of from the first match.
